description: Represent unsolved target-direction obligations as defects on a locally Euclidean product graph and import sweep-decoder intuition for moving them. A local CA should transport these defects until they annihilate or condense into a single legal (1,-1) singleton, after which exact arithmetic verification takes over.
mathematical_formalization: Assign to each unsolved local relation a defect charge q_v\in\mathbb{Z}^2. A local transport rule \sigma updates q by moving charge downhill relative to an orientation or height function h. Accept only if repeated transport yields \sum_v q_v=(1,-1)e_u for some u and the transport history can be realized by legal certificate operations.
analogical_connections: Syndrome defects in a topological code correspond to target-direction residues in the relation lattice.
Sweep rules become directed cancellation schedules for arithmetic defects.
Decoder locality offers a template for scalable, geometry-aware proof propagation.
implementation_hypothesis: Build a defect representation on the product grid and test local transport rules inspired by Sweep and self-dual decoders. For each successful transport pattern, compile its moves into relation operations and compute the true score improvement.
experiment_seed: Begin on 3D-free geometries such as 2D product grids with a chosen orientation and compare transport depth, seed count, and exact extractability. Keep only rules whose local transport meaningfully reduces seed count or edge overhead versus direct elimination.

novelty_claim: The new step is defect transport in an integer relation lattice compiled into arithmetic Kakeya witnesses, not generic decoding of physical noise.
differentiation: No cited decoder is designed for singleton-supported integer relations or the score (m+r)/(n-t). The analogy is operational only if transport moves survive exact compilation into the verifier's rule set.
